# Hyprune SDK · IPC 0.1–0.23

TypeScript/JavaScript client, `hyprune-mock` development daemon, and `hyprune` author/debug CLI. MIT. **SDK `0.6.1`: typed clients for IPC 0.1–0.23 (`new HypruneClient({protocol:'0.23', ...})`); default clients and the mock speak IPC `0.2`.** World formats 0.1–0.9 are typed and validated; extension and screen manifests remain `0.1`. Object and library manifests 0.9 (draft 0.10) are typed and checked by `hyprune object check` and `hyprune library check`. Schemas are vendored from [hyprune/schema at 7471481](https://github.com/hyprune/schema/tree/74714810717690b1b918118669965ace5d849fbe).
<!-- /header -->

> **Hyprune** is an explorable, world-driven desktop environment for Hyprland: your workspaces become places you can walk through, with live windows on the walls. This repository is the **SDK**: a TypeScript IPC client, the `hyprune` CLI for world and extension authors, and a mock daemon. Install Hyprune through the [hyprune](https://github.com/hyprune/hyprune) repository (starter kits, Nix, Arch); learn more at [hyprune.com](https://hyprune.com). Licence: MIT.

## Install

```sh
npm i -g @hyprune/sdk                  # or npx @hyprune/sdk ... / a project devDependency
hyprune world validate path/to/world   # schema, files, glTF and provenance checks
hyprune world pack path/to/world       # deterministic .tar.zst (needs GNU tar and zstd)
hyprune ext new widget my-widget       # scaffold an extension
hyprune-mock --demo                    # development daemon with a moving observatory
```

As a library: `import { HypruneClient } from '@hyprune/sdk'` (Node >= 22.12 or Bun). The schemas and validator alone are published as [`@hyprune/schema`](https://github.com/hyprune/schema).
RFC-0007 chooses JavaScript as the first reference client. TypeScript supplies generated types and compiles to JavaScript for **Node >=22.12 and Bun**; Python is used only by the core test harness. Quickshell needs its own native socket bridge; Node modules cannot be imported directly into QML.

Schemas and their Node validator are vendored unchanged (`vendor/schema/source.json`), with SHA-256 verification. Builds neither follow sibling repositories nor fetch schemas. `npm run generate` derives method, result, event, state and manifest types for every vendored protocol, and this README's header from the same pins. The former `0.1-mock.1` contract has been removed.

## First real session

SDK 0.3.0 adds explicit IPC `0.3` clients and generated spatial/workspace/binding
types. Existing default clients and the mock remain IPC 0.2. Use
`new HypruneClient({protocol:'0.3', ...})` for core's first-session contract.
`../core/dev/hyprune-dev up|smoke|record` starts the locked nested real session.
The core launcher consumes the built Switchyard package, starts core and shell
with one-use FD tokens, and supplies terminal/btop/browser apps. It never uses
the SDK mock. See core/docs/FIRST-SESSION.md for reproduction and evidence.

## Run the mock

```sh
npm ci
npm test
npm run mock -- --socket "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hyprune/sdk-demo/control.sock" --demo
```

This launches the moving observatory, a real `/proc` system-pulse publisher and a terminal widget. Use a private development socket. Ctrl+C stops the supervised examples and daemon; `--duration 5` bounds a demo. Socket defaults require a valid session environment; there is no fallback to `/tmp`.

For shell warp-overlay development:

```sh
npm run mock -- --socket "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hyprune/sdk-warp/control.sock" \
  --scenario scenarios/warp.json --demo --duration 4
```

The scenario starts a timed warp at 700 ms and a world load at 1700 ms. Both use real `0.2` methods and `location.transition` state/events. Replace `--demo --duration 4` with `--client-id org.example.shell --capabilities state.read,shell.control,movement.control,world.control --launch /path/to/shell-executable` to supervise a shell instead. The child must request the granted capabilities through its own hello.

The mock supports all 26 methods: camera, waypoint/routes, travel/autodrive, owned UI leases, world loading and data publication, plus the original methods. It serves seven revisioned state keys and exact five-key legacy projections. `--protocol 0.1` selects a legacy-only listener. It is trusted developer tooling; simulation does not replace core collision, rendering or authorization.

## CLI

After `npm ci`, use `npm run hyprune -- …`, or `npm link` to expose both executables:

```sh
hyprune world validate examples/world-minimal
hyprune world pack examples/world-minimal --output /path/to/minimal.tar.zst
hyprune object check path/to/street-lantern   # RFC-0011 object directory
hyprune library check path/to/com.example.street
hyprune ext new widget ./my-widget --id org.example.mywidget
hyprune ext new screen-type ./my-screen
hyprune ext new movement-mode ./my-movement
hyprune ext new integration ./my-integration
hyprune-mock --socket "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hyprune/sdk-test/control.sock" \
  --launch hyprune ipc subscribe --count 10
hyprune-mock --socket "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hyprune/sdk-test/control.sock" \
  --launch hyprune ipc call session.ping '{}'
hyprune-mock --socket "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hyprune/sdk-test/control.sock" \
  --launch hyprune doctor
```

World validation combines the upstream schema/semantic validator with file, provenance and Khronos glTF checks. `object check` and `library check` apply the same file and glTF checks to RFC-0011 object directories and libraries, plus thumbnail, texture and GPU-budget measurements (docs/world-tools.md). Packing produces a deterministic single-root `.tar.zst`; GNU tar and zstd are required. Runtime collision/spawn clearance and final GPU allocation remain core checks.

### Personal quests and focus sessions (IPC 0.21)

```sh
hyprune quest add "Write the release notes" --step Draft --focus 2 --step Review
hyprune quest list                       # * marks the tracked quest
hyprune quest track write-the-release-notes
hyprune quest done write-the-release-notes step-1 [objectiveId]
hyprune quest rm write-the-release-notes
hyprune focus start --work 50 --break 10 --cycles 2 --workspace 21
hyprune focus pause|resume|skip|stop|status
```

One `--step` per step (ids default to `step-1`, `step-2`, …; a quest without `--step`
gets one step named after it). `--focus N` gives the step named by the `--step` before
it a focus objective of N sessions; without any `--step` it applies to the quest's single
step. Steps without `--focus` get a manual objective (`done`), marked with `quest done`.
Also: `quest show <id>`, `quest untrack`, `quest abandon|resume <id>`, `--summary`,
`--expires YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, `--any-order` (non-sequential), `--state <state>` for
`list`, and `focus start --app CLASS` (with `--workspace`: that window class on that
workspace), `--long-break MIN`, `--quest <id> [--objective <id>]`. `--json` prints the
raw results. These commands speak IPC 0.21 unless `--protocol`/`HYPRUNE_PROTOCOL` names
a newer pin, and request `state.read` plus the `quest.control` grant.
To try them against the mock:

```sh
hyprune-mock --protocol 0.21 --socket "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hyprune/sdk-test/control.sock" \
  --capabilities state.read,quest.control --launch hyprune quest list
```

### User objects and libraries (IPC 0.22)

```sh
hyprune object add ./street-lantern                  # a checked object directory
hyprune object add ./lamp.glb --license CC0-1.0 --author "Example Author" [--name Lamp] [--surface floor|wall|ceiling|any]
hyprune object list [--json]                         # objects.catalog
hyprune library install ./com.example.street-1.2.0.tar.zst
hyprune library install com.example.street@1.2.0 --releases libraries/releases.json [--archive file.tar.zst]
hyprune library list [--json]
hyprune library remove com.example.street@1.2.0
```

`object add` writes only to the user object folder: `$HYPRUNE_OBJECT_DIR`, else
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/hyprune/objects`, else `~/.local/share/hyprune/objects`. A directory is
copied as `<id>/` (its `object.json` id, whatever the source directory is called); a bare
`.glb` gets a minimal `object.json` (format 0.9, id from the file name, version 1.0.0,
category `other`, bounds measured from the glTF accessors, `traits.movable` on the given
surface, default `floor`); `--license` and `--author` are required for it. The copy is
staged in a `.hyprune-add-*` directory next to the target, checked with `validateObject`
and renamed into place, so core's folder watch never sees a half-written object; a
failing check writes nothing, and a bare `.glb` reports its first failure. An existing
`<id>/` needs `--replace`. The folder holds at most 256 objects.

`library install` never downloads: a local archive is hashed and handed to core as
`libraries.install {archive, sha256}` (core re-hashes, extracts and validates it);
`id@version` looks up a `library-releases` record (`--releases`, the meta repository's
`libraries/releases.json` format) and uses `--archive` or the archive named by the
record's URL (or `<id>-<version>.tar.zst`) next to the record, which must match the
pinned hash. `object list`, `library list|install|remove` speak IPC 0.22 unless
`--protocol`/`HYPRUNE_PROTOCOL` names a newer pin; `list` requests `state.read`,
install/remove also the `objects.control` grant. To try them against the mock:

```sh
hyprune-mock --protocol 0.22 --object-dir "$HOME/.local/share/hyprune/objects" \
  --socket "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hyprune/sdk-test/control.sock" \
  --capabilities state.read,objects.control --launch hyprune object list
```

### Characters and paths (IPC 0.23)

```sh
hyprune npc list [--json]                            # character instances (+ npcs state with --json)
hyprune npc spawn library/com.hyprune.starter@0.1.0/resident-blue --path gallery-loop [--phase 0.5] [--speed 1.2] [--accent 0.9,0.4,0.1] [--reverse]
hyprune npc spawn user/my-character                  # standing in front of the player
hyprune npc disable|enable <id>                      # authored and user characters
hyprune npc remove <id> | --all                      # user characters
hyprune path list [--json]                           # package and user paths, walkability, bound characters
```

`--path` is a `route` (`package/<id>` or `user/<id>`; a bare id means `package/<id>`).
The commands speak IPC 0.23 unless `--protocol`/`HYPRUNE_PROTOCOL` names a newer pin;
`list` requests `state.read`, the others also `objects.control`. Drawing a route with
tool 3 (`paths.draw`/`paths.finish`) is a shell flow; the mock simulates it (see
[mock](docs/mock.md)).

Tokens are passed through a one-use inherited FD, never command arguments or logs. The mock supervisor approves `--capabilities`; the CLI independently requests its `--capabilities`. Debug commands accept `--protocol 0.1` for a legacy daemon; default is `0.2`. An unauthenticated connection may hello/ping only.

## Library

Run under an authorized supervisor supplying `HYPRUNE_TOKEN_FD`, `HYPRUNE_SOCKET`, `HYPRUNE_CLIENT_ID` and `HYPRUNE_PROTOCOL`:

```ts
import { clientFromEnvironment } from '@hyprune/sdk';
const client = clientFromEnvironment({ protocol: '0.2', capabilities: ['state.read'] });
client.on('state', snapshot => console.log(snapshot.state.location.transition));
client.on('location.transition', event => console.log(event.phase, event.progress));
await client.connect();
await client.subscribe();
console.log(await client.call('camera.get', {}));
client.close();
```

`HypruneClient` validates against the negotiated schema, reduces whole-key deltas, resyncs gaps and reconnects with exponential backoff and a fresh-token callback. It takes a fresh snapshot after reconnect and **never retries mutations**. The inherited-FD helper disables reconnect; long-lived callers must supply a supervisor callback and enable reconnect. Presentation events are hints; revisioned state is authoritative.

System-pulse now uses the real `data.publish` grant/method, increasing sequences and TTL. The widget reads `state.integrations.sources`. The extension manifest schema cannot yet declare `data.publish`: the demo uses a separate, explicitly trusted `launch.json`. This is documented in [the remaining RFC gaps](https://github.com/hyprune/sdk/blob/main/NOTES-rfc-gaps.md), alongside the sandbox metrics broker and production supervisor work.

```sh
HYPRUNE_CORE_BINARY=/path/to/core/build/hypruned npm test
```

Local verification: **52/52 Node tests with built core**, **50/50 Bun tests**, and **4/4 core CTest tests**. The core harness launches real `hypruned` and links actual core `Control`, simulation and world-loading code behind a private plugin stand-in. It starts no compositor and touches no owner session. ## M3A hands-on desktop contract

Use `new HypruneClient({protocol:'0.5', ...})` for revisioned `interaction` mode,
selected tool, five slots, noclip and cursor state, plus workspace `apps` metadata.
Custom mounts include metre pose/size with an empty authored anchor ID. IPC 0.4
mount methods and generated types are also available. StateStore validates the
negotiated exact snapshot/delta before installation; old contracts remain isolated.
The mock continues to implement IPC 0.1/0.2 only. Rendering, hand input, cursor
ownership and Lua config validation belong to core; see core/docs/M3A.md.

IPC 0.6 clients opt in with `protocol: '0.6'`. Generated types cover independent
keymap v2 config, core-side preview/save and verified Director capture, plus mode,
tool/submode, paths and object transforms. Request `input.control` for writes.
Older versions and the default 0.2 stay unchanged. The mock remains a 0.2 world
simulator; native input stealing and capture require real core nested tests.


IPC 0.7 adds typed graphics discovery/persistence (`graphics.get`/`graphics.set`);
IPC 0.8 adds `keymap.holds` timing for local shell animation. Pass an explicit
protocol to `HypruneClient`; defaults and earlier shapes remain unchanged.
Generated types and offline validators are pinned to schema e0739d1. The mock
still supports its existing scenarios; this update does not claim a GPU mock.

IPC **0.11** adds climbing movement activity; **0.12** adds private recording and
fixed-step/camera replay. The generated `ClimbingMethodMap` and
`RecordingMethodMap` inherit all older methods. Recording/replay methods require
`input.control`; keystrokes delivered to apps are masked by default. Use
`recording.start`, `recording.mark`, `recording.stop`, and `replay.start` with an
optional assertion spec. Camera mode accepts `smoothingMs` and never types into
apps. Schemas now pin canonical schema `153d4d8` including world format 0.4.

Unreleased IPC 0.12 includes `cursor` interaction/editor mode and the world
free-cursor toggle. Schema pin: `011bcd0db8eccf5b5392e20a308aa84e0ff8e1a4`.

IPC **0.13** exposes `camera.photo`/`camera.release` only with a trusted dev
`camera.author` grant, actual roll/FOV/lens shift in camera.get, and Performance
controls `outline`/`visibility_culling`. Normal shell grants omit camera.author.
Generated world 0.5 types describe optional ink and directed visibility regions;
the package validator checks node bounds and conflicting subtree ownership.

IPC **0.14** adds `graphics.outline_quality: "fast" | "smooth" | null` to
`graphics.set` and Performance data. Null inherits the preset. Fast is a fixed
1 logical px stroke; smooth honours the world's outline width (1–4 logical px).
Core performs the effect at internal world resolution before native app surfaces.

Use `graphics.set` with nullable `outline_width_px` (1–4) and `outline_colour`
(RGB triplet, 0–1) for persistent user overrides. Null restores the current world
style. `atmosphere.set` is a transient preview, not a settings persistence API.

IPC `0.15` adds the four shared tool bindings (`primary`, `secondary`,
`alternate`, `cycle`) and generic `editor.toolSlots` / `toolDefinitions`, plus
`editor.unplaced`, carry-facing and content-scale feedback. Placement 5's
Alternate pockets the aimed window; it does not restore an old spot. Older
protocols retain their frozen keymap/state projection.

World validation also accepts format **0.6** (`World06_Document`): world/area
playable boxes or convex hulls, maximum fly height, and declared backdrop cards.
`validateWorld()` reports CLAMP_TO_EDGE warnings for far-card texture samplers;
core remains authoritative for flight, collision and renderer behavior.

World format **0.7** (`World07_Document`) keeps the 0.6 manifest and allows
compressed scene assets: `KHR_texture_basisu` KTX2 material textures,
`EXT_meshopt_compression` and `KHR_mesh_quantization`. `validateWorld` applies
the shared schema `scene` check (required glTF extensions by world format, PNG
lightmaps) and drops the bundled glTF validator's KTX2 "unknown image"
warnings, which predate the extension. Vendored schema: `6250450`.

World format **0.8** (`World08_Document`, `World08_ObjectAssets`, `World08_Objects`)
adds placed world objects: object assets (package glTFs with optional
`spin`/`orbit`/`bob` node animation, a static collision proxy and `probe`/`unlit`
lighting) and their instances (pose, scale, speed, phase, optional ambient).
`validateWorld` checks each asset's glTF like the scene (extension rules, safe
resources, the Khronos validator) plus the shared asset rules (node names,
animation nesting, collision proxy); `library` references are reserved and
rejected. Core stays authoritative for rendering, probe lighting and proxies
(RFC-0004 "world 0.8").

World format **0.9** (`World09_Document`, RFC-0004 "world 0.9", RFC-0011 P2) adds
characters, paths, seats and `keepClear`. Object assets take exactly one source: inline
(`scene` plus optional `traits` and `slots`; `animations` and `collision` stay as
shorthand), `dir` (a package object directory) or `library` + `object`
(`<reverse-domain id>@<semver>`). Instances gain `path` (a `route` path, instead of
`pose`), `reverse`, `seat`, `accent`, `interactions` (`say`, `waypoint`, `guide`,
`panel`) and `locked`; top-level `paths` (`route`, `track` or `generic`, `line`/`curve`/
`arc` points, stops), `seats` and `keepClear` are new. `validateWorld` checks `dir`
assets as object directories and passes their `object.json` to the shared validator
(`options.assets`) for the character, seat and movable rules; `library` assets are
resolved by core against installed libraries and only reported. Route walkability and
seat reachability stay with core and `hyprune-world-check` (see
[world tools](docs/world-tools.md)).

IPC **0.16** (`HypruneClient<'0.16'>`) adds the typed `upscaler` graphics setting
(`'fsr1' | 'bilinear' | null`). `PROTOCOLS` in `validation.ts` is the single runtime
list of negotiable protocols; `Protocol` is derived from it. Vendored schema `1ae2ed1`.

IPC **0.17** (`HypruneClient<'0.17'>`) adds debug capture notes: the
`capture.taken` notification (`{captureId, timestampMs, mode}`) and
`capture.annotate {captureId, note}` (shell.control; 0-1000 code points, no control
characters). `PROTOCOLS` and the method maps follow the vendored pins. Vendored
schema `2041dff`.

IPC **0.18** (`HypruneClient<'0.18'>`) scales the offload power cap to the device:
`offload_power_cap_w` is `number | null` (20-1000 W; `null` = automatic, the new
default) and `offload_device` is `'auto'` or a lowercase PCI address such as
`'0000:65:00.0'`. `graphics.get/set` Performance records add `capSource`
(`'profile' | 'device' | 'configured' | 'fallback'`) and `device` (`null` or
`{pci, node, name, enforcedLimitW, selection, drivesCompositor}`). Vendored schema
`53c86f4`.

IPC **0.19** (`HypruneClient<'0.19'>`) adds typed player settings: `player.get {}`
(state.read) and `player.set {patch}` (movement.control) return `{config, defaults,
overrides, options, ranges, path, error}` for walk/run speed, view bob, reticle
style/size/thickness/gap/opacity/outline/colour/dynamic and the grab/mount/placement
reach limits (`null` in a patch drops the override). Graphics `fov` goes to 120,
`overlay.style` gains `reticleColor`/`validColor`/`invalidColor` and
`state.interaction.reticle {state, action}` is required. Everything else, including
the 0.18 offload keys, is inherited. Vendored schema `f76922b`.

IPC **0.20** (`HypruneClient<'0.20'>`) adds `surface.pocket {surfaceId}` and
`surface.unpocket {surfaceId}` (surface.control): put a world window into the pocket
and take it out again (`{revision, placed}`; `placed: false` leaves it selected for
the Placement tool). Pocket membership is `state.editor.unplaced.windows`.
`state.spatial.map.levels` (optional) carries the world's blueprint levels
`{id, name, minY, maxY, svg, sha256}`. Vendored schema `d5db513`.

IPC **0.21** (`HypruneClient<'0.21'>`, RFC-0012 P1) adds markers, personal quests and
focus sessions. State gains `markers` (reveal, persistent mode, calm, `coreDraw`, up to
64 resolved markers), `quests` (tracked, up to 16 active, counts) and `focus` (phase,
monotonic phase times, credit, cycles, target). Methods: `markers.reveal`
(shell.control), `guidance.get`/`guidance.set`, `quests.list/get/track/accept/abandon/
resume/create/update/delete/mark` and `focus.start/pause/resume/skip/stop/history`;
mutations need the new `quest.control` grant. Events `quest.progress` and `focus.phase`.
The world keymap gains `markers.reveal`, the overlay style `questColor`, projection
markers an optional `markerId`. `hyprune-mock --protocol 0.21` simulates them in memory
(see [mock](docs/mock.md)), and the CLI has `quest` and `focus` commands (above).
Vendored schema `669a259`.

IPC **0.22** (`HypruneClient<'0.22'>`, RFC-0011 P1) adds the object catalog, user
placements and libraries. State gains `objects` (`catalogRevision`, up to 512 instances
of this world: authored first, then user placements `u-xxxxxx`, each with its committed
pose, scale, state, `movable`, `locked` and the blocking `rule`; up to 16 object pocket
items; user-placement `usage` against `limits`). Methods: `objects.catalog` (up to 1,024
entries from the world package, installed libraries and the user folder, with
`placeable` and a `reason`), `objects.pocket/place/transform/remove/hide/reset/configure`
and `libraries.list/install/remove`; changes need the new `objects.control` grant. Refs
are `package/<asset>`, `library/<id>@<version>/<object>` or `user/<object>`. A refused
placement is `-32007` with `error.data.rule` (`playable`, `walls`, `support`, `window`,
`approach`, `zone`, `keep-clear`, `player`, `reach`, or `library.conflict`), a budget
`-32008` with rule `budget`; `RpcError.data.rule` carries it. The editor gains
`selectedKind: "node"`, the `universal` submode, `unplaced.objects` and `gizmo
{space, pivot, snap}`. No new events; notices use new codes (`object.placed`,
`library.installed`, …). `hyprune-mock --protocol 0.22` simulates all of it (see
[mock](docs/mock.md)), and the CLI has `object add|list` and `library
install|list|remove` (above). Vendored schema `ce517ea`.

IPC **0.23** (`HypruneClient<'0.23'>`, RFC-0010/RFC-0011 P2) adds characters, paths and
interactions. State gains the required `npcs` key (`motion` setting, effective `state`
and pause `reason`, authored/user `usage` and `limits` 16/8, the `drawing` in progress,
the `aimed` character and the running `interaction` or choice list); object instances
gain `character` and `accent`, and `path` (`package/<id>` or `user/<id>`), `activity`
and `seat` carry values; `editor.paths` gain `use`, `name`, `speed` and `stops`; the
reticle action may be `interact`; `graphics.get/set` gain `npc_motion`
(`auto|always|still|off`). Methods: `npcs.spawn/bind/disable/remove`,
`paths.set/remove/draw/finish` (objects.control), `paths.list` (state.read) and
`interaction.choose` (world.control); there is no new grant or event. Refusals: -32004
unknown id/ref/path, -32005 protected, authored or not a character, -32007 rule
`walkable` (or a placement rule), -32008 rule `budget` (8 user characters per world);
characters are refused by `objects.transform/configure/pocket` and `objects.place`.
Notices use new codes (`npc.spawned`, `path.unwalkable`, …). `hyprune-mock --protocol
0.23` simulates it in memory (see [mock](docs/mock.md)), and the CLI has `npc` and `path`
commands (above). Peers below 0.23 keep their exact shapes. Vendored schema `50d7271`.
